$comment: Works taken down, one entry per work id. THIS FILE IS THE TAKEDOWN LEVER.
docs/decisions.md's Architecture consequences require that 'any work can be
individually unpublished or degraded to a link-out to vatican.va without
rearchitecting'. This is that mechanism, and it is deliberately a data file
rather than code: responding to a rights holder should be an edit and a
deploy by whoever is awake, not a patch.
Adding an entry withholds everything derived from the work: its reading
text AND its structure tree. sync-corpus.mjs stops writing both, so they
are absent from the build rather than hidden by the client. Only the
manifest survives — title, language, rights holder's notice, source URL —
which is bibliographic data about the work, not the work.
WHAT THE READER GETS: the work's landing page still exists and renders a
notice naming the work, the reason, the rights holder's own copyright
line, and a link to the page on vatican.va the text came from. Listings
mark it rather than hiding it, because a silently vanished document looks
like a bug and invites someone to 'fix' it.
WHAT BREAKS, STATED PLAINLY: per-section URLs (/documents/{slug}/{n}) stop
being generated, because the structure they are enumerated from is gone.
An external bookmark to a section lands on the site's 404 rather than on
the notice. Links from INSIDE the site do not break — refs.ts asks
documentSectionExists before linking, which now answers false, so CCC
citations quietly stop linking instead of pointing at nothing, and the
build stays green under prerender's handleHttpError: 'fail'. Routing every
section URL to the notice would need the section numbers kept, which is a
deliberate trade not taken: addresses are cheap to keep, but keeping them
means keeping a map of the work's internal divisions, and a takedown
request is not an invitation to negotiate over how much we hold back.
Keyed by WORK ID ('encyclical.laudato-si.en'), not by slug, because a
request may concern one language edition and not another. Taking down a
document in both languages means two entries.
Example entry, with the fields the notice renders:
"encyclical.laudato-si.en": {
"reason": "Requested by the rights holder, 2026-08-16."
